text: Twenty videos, one engagement: Brennan Manufacturing, whose production-scheduling database just went dark for two days. We start where this always starts -- not with a cluster, with the meeting.

A nine-year-old single server, SQLPROD01, had no secondary of any kind. Its RAID controller failed, the replacement part took two days to arrive, and a never-rehearsed bare-metal restore cost the second day on its own.
The real cost: about four hours of lost order data, twelve orders that missed their ship date, and one production line running off a whiteboard, burning six hours on avoidable changeovers.
Three honest accounts matter: Dana Kowalski wants this to never happen again, Marcus Webb's lines run blind without the schedule, and Greg Hollis has kept this server alive alone for nine years.
The incident is documented and confirmed. Next: turning 'make it resilient' into actual numbers everyone is building toward.
